verdict.justification: Both deliverables demonstrate strong GMP domain knowledge and catch subtle nuances in the source documents, such as the COA reporting '< 5 EU/ml' (which fails to prove '< 1 EU/ml'), the contradictory 'only report the results' wording in RMS-3333, and the expiry rule conflict. However, Deliverable B is more thorough, structured, and operationally sound across all documents. In the Risk Assessment, Deliverable B follows ICH Q9(R1) principles, provides a concrete Severity x Likelihood scoring matrix, maps every mitigation action (M1-M14) directly to specific risk IDs (R1-R7), and includes a residual risk evaluation, whereas Deliverable A leaves four of its seven risks unrated as 'Unknown' / 'To be rated'. Deliverable B also catches a critical chronological discrepancy in the reference material: the COA was released on 29 May 2025 already showing 'Report Result', indicating the vendor may have implemented the change before sending the notification. Furthermore, in the QA Escalation Email, Deliverable B properly utilizes the specific personnel names from RMS-3333 ('Sam Heaburts (QA - approver, RMS-3333); Alec Grace (MSAT - author, RMS-3333)'), whereas Deliverable A leaves generic placeholders.
